limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES (issue #1705): that the gate's last stderr line, FLOW_FINISH_GATE_EXIT=<n>, does not report a clean or stale status for a gate that was killed before it announced an exit. The line is read by sessions other than the one that ran the gate (ADR 0008's bound: a check whose green is read by a different session always needs a control). The bad case starts the gate with a runner stub that blocks, sends SIGTERM to the gate's pid ALONE once the runner is up, and reads the line: the gate must have written 128 (run-case.sh then answers 'unannounced', exit 1). The good case runs the gate into a deliberate exit - a usage error, exit 2 - and the line must read that status: a gate or mutant that printed 128 for an ANNOUNCED exit (a worse lie than the one fixed) answers 'unannounced' on the good case and so fails it. good_signal requires run-case.sh's own 'status <n>' answer, so a good verdict is something the runner said and not merely exit 0; it deliberately does not pin the number, because the anchor's MISS on the bad case is 'status 0' and has to read as the clean answer for the harness to score it blind. THE ANCHOR is the script at 3eaf643d, before #1705: it prints 0 for the killed gate, so it misses the bad case. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which signal killed the gate (128 is one fixed value by design; the process's real exit status carries the signal, and run-case.sh checks that status is 143 as a precondition, refusing as cannot-run otherwise). It exercises SIGTERM to the pid alone, not a group kill, SIGINT or SIGHUP (those are in tests/test_flow_finish_gate.py), not an abort that is not a signal, not the coordination status-file path, and not the Makefile fallback lane. It does not show the line is LAST on stderr: on a group kill bash appends its own job notice after the EXIT trap has run (measured on the pre-#1705 script too). The gate is staged in an isolated directory with the CURRENT scripts/gate-lib.sh beside it, so the anchor runs against today's library; a future change to gate-lib that the old script cannot load would make the anchor unrunnable, and run-case.sh would then report cannot-run instead of a verdict. uv is a stub on PATH; no runner, network or repository is involved.
